'''Lev Nikolaevich Lipatov''' ({{langx|ru|Лев Никола́евич Липа́тов}}; 2 May 1940, in [[Leningrad]] – 4 September 2017, in [[Dubna]])<ref name="RAS">[http://www.ras.ru/win/db/show_per.asp?P=.id-610.ln-ru Russian Academy of Sciences]</ref> was a Russian physicist, well known for his contributions to [[nuclear physics]] and particle physics. He has been the head of Theoretical Physics Division <ref>[http://thd.pnpi.spb.ru/ Theoretical Division of PNPI]</ref> at St. Petersburg's Nuclear Physics Institute of Russian Academy of Sciences in [[Gatchina]] and an Academician of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="RAS"/>

For the long period he worked with [[Vladimir Gribov]], laying a basis for a field theory description of [[deep inelastic scattering]] and annihilation (Gribov-Lipatov evolution equations, later known as [[DGLAP]], 1972). He wrote significant papers of the Pomeranchuk singularity in [[quantum chromodynamics]] (1977) what resulted in deriving the Balitsky–Fadin–Kuraev–Lipatov (BFKL) evolution equation (after Ian Balitsky, [[Victor Fadin]], [[Eduard A. Kuraev]] and Lipatov),  contributed to the study of critical phenomena (semiclassical Lipatov's approximation), the theory of tunnelling and [[renormalon]] contribution to effective couplings. He discovered the connection between high-energy scattering and the [[Integrable system#Exactly solvable models|exactly solvable models]] (1994). HEJA BVB
